newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bund futures hit record as gloom prevails.
newsitem.headline: German bund futures hit record as gloom prevails.

text.p: German bond futures eased in late trade after storming to a record high in mid-session, as the general gloom about Germany's mass unemployment and economic outlook made bonds look increasingly attractive.
Traders said the market was quiet -- with volumes hurt by pre-Lent carnival holidays across Germany and a half-holiday in Frankfurt -- but that the mood was extremely positive.

The bund future jumped 0.30 point to 102.95, ending below a new record high of 103.02. Despite the positive outlook for the market, traders said it looked toppish at these levels and took the opportunity to book profits.
Dealers said that the further direction of the market would depend on the upcoming U.S. quarterly refunding, with any impact from that on the Treasuries market having a knock-on effect here.
The benchmark six percent January 2007 Bund ended at 103.13, for a yield of 5.58 percent, up from 102.88.
